attribution_limitations: Case 1 report states eculizumab among the immunosuppressive agents given before the return visit, yet later says the patient was subsequently started on eculizumab 900 mg IV weekly. The source does not reconcile the two; no order or restart is inferred.

Case 1 states that no complement regulatory gene mutations were identified. The Discussion says "the other patient" (not Patient 2) did not undergo genetic testing; that sentence names no patient and reaches Patient 1 only by exclusion, so it is review_only and is not treated as a source conflict. The Case 1 statement stays included.
The CT finding is thought to be secondary to myocarditis or multivessel ischemia; the source asserts neither, and the later normal coronary angiogram is not linked to either by the source.

The antiphospholipid antibody sentence gives anticardiolipin (47 SGU) and anti-beta 2 glycoprotein (30 GPL) values under one "elevated" and one IgG isotype mention; the coordinated phrase is read as covering both antibodies. The units are printed the other way round from the Patient 2 history (anticardiolipin IgG in GPL, anti-beta 2 glycoprotein IgG in SGU); values and units are kept as printed and not corrected.

The Discussion says both patients developed acute severe diffuse global hypokinesis and that coronary angiography was unrevealing in both cases; Case 1 text reports severe global hypokinesis and normal coronary arteries, so these Discussion sentences are not copied as additional facts.

patients.label: Case 2: 57-year-old man with SLE and antiphospholipid syndrome, catastrophic antiphospholipid antibody syndrome and dilated cardiomyopathy
attribution_limitations: Case 2 reports ADAMTS13 activity abnormal at 34%, while the Discussion says TTP was ruled out in each patient on the basis of normal ADAMTS13 activity. Only the abnormal/normal status is quarantined: the 34% value is kept with an unknown flag, the Discussion "normal" flag is review_only, and the stated TTP ruling-out is kept.
Case 2 says continuous renal replacement therapy was started, but later says he did not require dialysis; the source does not reconcile the two statements.
The source says concern for CAPS versus ITP prompted therapy; it asserts neither diagnosis at that point.

The Discussion describes both patients as having CAPS with clinicopathologic signs of TMA, but specifies clinicopathologic evidence of TMA "in those biopsied"; no biopsy is documented for Case 2, so only the case text's high suspicion of CAPS-associated TMA is recorded for this patient.

The history lists ITP treatment as "status post IVIG and four cycles of cyclophosphamide, rituximab, dexamethasone, prednisone, and romiplistin"; whether "four cycles" applies to every drug is not stated and no cycle counts are recorded.
The scope of "treated with antibiotic therapy" over the three listed infections is not stated, so no indication is recorded for the antibiotic fact.

The Discussion says both developed acute severe diffuse global hypokinesis and that coronary angiogram was unrevealing in both; Case 2 reports moderate diffuse hypokinesis with regional severe hypokinesis and single vessel disease of the first diagonal branch. The Discussion generalisation is not copied as extra facts.

The variant description for the second listed mutation string is glued and internally inconsistent in print, and genetic methods in the Discussion are described for patient samples generally; the second string is review-only and no method is attached to Patient 2 beyond the printed result.
